speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: asked the Minister for Health as the Ministry carries out its supervision priority for Cordlife to rectify their shortcomings pending the investigations, whether there are strategies in place to ensure that (i) there will be open and clear communication between Cordlife and the parents affected and (ii) affected parents are well informed on potential ramifications of their decision to transfer their cord blood units to another private cord blood bank backed by scientific evidence, should they opt to do so.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Cord blood banking is an elective, commercial service provided by the private sector.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Customers entered into a commercial contract with the service providers when they sign up and the Ministry of Health (MOH) is not a party to these contracts.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are limits to which the Government can intervene, especially when it comes to issues of compensation and refunds.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: What MOH is actively doing is with respect to regulation and facilitation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Given the sample sizes and the testing capacity available, this will take another year.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MOH will also closely monitor Cordlife's dissemination of information to its customers and the public, as well as progress in addressing the deficiencies identified and in making improvements.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These include directing Cordlife to properly validate and implement its new temperature monitoring system, revalidate its processing method for cord blood units and enhance staff training and supervision of its operations more closely.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MOH has also discussed with other providers who are prepared to facilitate transfer of their cord blood units.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Parents who wish to do so can contact Cordlife and the receiving cord blood bank to discuss the transfer arrangements.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That said, we urge parents to carefully consider the risks of doing so, given the logistical complexity of making a physical transfer at sub-zero temperatures, particularly so when the cord blood is not ascertained to be impacted.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I understand that MOH has more supervisory and regulatory authority in this case.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Senior Minister of State highlighted about the one-year duration which, understandably, is causing parents even further anxiety, given the long wait.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What is the Ministry's assessment on the reasonableness of this one-year duration for completing the remaining testing?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is there any other way that MOH can provide direction or support for other industry partners to expedite the testing of the cord blood units?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There has been some commentary about the length of time that is projected.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The comments provided by some international experts are based on the typical turnaround time for routine testing and samples that are already in a laboratory.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think some people have quoted two to three weeks for a single potency test and returning the results.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But that series of comments does not take into account the other related factors and the full context of this case.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The resources that Cordlife has, the resources that are available at the third-party laboratory that has been engaged to perform the testing and the rectification measures that Cordlife has been instructed to put in place to mitigate further warming events, the limited resources that the laboratory and Cordlife have, as well as what MOH needs to do in terms of assessing these processes, those parts of the explanation that are under our control, we will try to minimise the time taken, expedite the process, but maintain the quality of our findings.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We need the process to be robust so that when the findings are validated, there is a high level of confidence in that validation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Perhaps, I might just explain why it takes so long.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are several stages for what is called the post-thaw study.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These have to be designed carefully, the samples have to be retrieved very carefully, the testing has to be done very carefully and the third parties, the people who are validating and auditing this, also need to be satisfied that the samples are being dealt with in the proper manner.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: A cord blood unit is not stored in an individual tank.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The storage units contain many, many cord blood units.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They were retrieved and stored under different conditions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the sampling needs to take into account the processing methods at the time of freezing.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The way in which the retrieval is done has to be very, very careful because you do not want, in the course of establishing the potency of the unit, to then invalidate the potency of that sample.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, you have to make sure that there is no inadvertent compromise to the cord blood unit.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And the testing laboratory needs to then have the capacity to immediately receive the sample.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, you cannot ship the whole unit and then let them take their own time to process all the samples.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Each sample has to have a specified time slot for receipt and processing so that they are not then subject to risks at the laboratory side.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And there is a limited capacity available for the testing.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The laboratories that can do this are quite limited.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is also no way to divide up a sample volume and send it out to different laboratories.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is only so much of the sample that is there.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We understand the need, from the parents' concerns, to expedite this to reassure people as fast as possible, but I think it is important that when the process is complete, that all who are involved have confidence in the findings from the process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, I would ask for Members and parents' understanding that it will take some time for us to go through this process.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: She said that they have been paying a premium for a service that has not met expectations and, had they been aware of the situation, they would have made very different choices today.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: As general mid-working-class citizens, $12,000 is a significant amount of money for them.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: They shared that the current compensation offered by Cordlife, which includes a refund of the annual fee of $250 per year and the waiver of further fees going forward, is, unfortunately, not sufficient and it does not include the initial contract fee, hence, my initial Parliamentary Question (PQ).

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: She told me that the token gesture does not address the fundamental issue at hand, which is the catastrophic failure of Cordlife's services, which has irreversibly compromised the viability of their twins' cord blood samples.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This is, given the quantum of claim and the likely legal costs involved, some parents may be deterred from engaging lawyers.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I take the point that the Senior Minister of State has shared which is that, even if, indeed, it is the case that the company is not legally obliged to respond to any Government efforts, I wish the Government can engage the company on this front.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If I understand the Member's position with respect to his first supplementary question, he recognises and agrees that these are contractual matters between the parents and Cordlife.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the role that we might play in the Government is to engage with Cordlife and ask them to facilitate some form of recompense to maintain their relationship with their customers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But as the Member has agreed and as he has highlighted, this is a contractual matter between two private parties, and MOH and the Government are not a party to these contracts.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As for the Member's second question about legislating further protection, I think we do have to study the regulatory lessons that have come out of this episode and to see whether or not such services need a further type of regulation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would say that this is one operator amongst several and I think this is one incident in that operator.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It does not automatically mean that the regulatory regime or the legislative framework is inherently wrong.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It may be issues about operationalising it and auditing it.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But, nevertheless, we will study this episode to see how we can make sure that there is confidence in the industry, going forward.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can I remind Members to keep your supplementary questions succinct?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Speaker, I thank Mr Saktiandi for the question.
So, there is some variance and the parents, the customers will have to work directly with the receiving cord blood banks to operationalise the transfer.
MOH will try to facilitate the connections and processes, where it is within our power to do so.
However, I would want to take this opportunity to point out a couple of points.
It is not a small decision to be taken lightly.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just one supplementary question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I note in the press release by Cordlife yesterday that they mentioned the remaining five tanks are deemed to be so-called "low risk" in terms of the viability of the cord blood units there.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In the testing that the Senior Minister of State mentioned, this one-year period, does it involve comprehensive testing of all the various tanks and units that are stored within Cordlife, and at the same time, also in the operational processes, to give parents the assurance that there is indeed a low risk of the remaining cord blood units being affected and so that there is greater confidence as to any potential future lapses by having this independent third-party audit of Cordlife's assurances?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The entire process is designed to provide a high level of confidence in the findings, to make sure that Cordlife themselves can demonstrate that they are doing the right thing and moving in the right direction to improve protections, and for confidence in the industry as a whole to be shored up.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: He had a specific question on the five tanks that were in the report.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do not have the information about exactly where those five tanks are in our overall assessment and the one-year timeline.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If he would like to, I can follow up with him separately on this.
